source_admission: Sources for the plan of 2026-10-02, each with what was read of it. None is imported or installed; source admission for the manuscripts is separate.

sources.use: Availability of double-moment mass/number output through output_q and Morrison fall-speed output through output_fallvel; actual saved fields require inspection.
sources.access: Relevant output-variable documentation read; the project's pinned CM1 r22.0 source and individual run control files remain authoritative for implementation.

sources.citation: Edward R. Mansell, MicroTed/wrf4-elec developer repository
sources.use: Existing WRF-ELEC candidate implementation; repository advertises beta versions for several WRF releases. No release selected for Terluna.
sources.access: Repository overview read; electrical implementation and build instructions have not been audited or installed.

sources.citation: Sun et al. (2021), Aerosol effects on electrification and lightning discharges in a multicell thunderstorm simulated by the WRF-ELEC model, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 21, 14141–14158
sources.use: Published example of NSSL double-moment microphysics, charging, electric-field solution and discharge parameterization; links between particle populations and charging.
sources.access: Abstract and model overview (section 2.3) read in the publisher's full text; the full paper has not received a systematic source review.

sources.citation: Pasko, Inan, Bell and Taranenko (1997), Sprites produced by quasi-electrostatic heating and ionization in the lower ionosphere, Journal of Geophysical Research 102(A3), 4529–4561
sources.use: Dependence of sprite response on removed storm charge, its height and timescale, and upper-atmosphere conductivity; motivates a separate response model.
sources.access: Author institution's abstract and bibliographic record read; full paper not reviewed.

sources.citation: Ebert et al. (2010), Review of recent results on streamer discharges and discussion of their relevance for sprites and lightning
sources.use: Gas-density scaling and the distinction between storm-scale modeling and detailed streamer propagation; follow-up reading for the TLE stage.
sources.access: Author-posted abstract read; full review not read for this plan.
